name: Learn: Config & Secrets
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration & Security. Drill EVERY way to feed config into pods: single-key env, bulk envFrom + prefix, volume mounts with items/subPath, Secrets (env + volume + types), immutable, projected volumes, and a no-hint diagnose-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Seven strict config practicals against pre-seeded ConfigMaps/Secrets. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Single-key env + an optional key
questions.teach:
**Single key → env var:** `env: [{name: X, valueFrom: {configMapKeyRef: {name: cm, key: K}}}]`. Add `optional: true` on a key ref so a **missing** key doesn't block pod start.

**Gotcha:** a referenced key that doesn't exist and isn't `optional` leaves the pod in `CreateContainerConfigError`.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `cfg-env` (`busybox:1.36`, `sh -c 'sleep 3600'`):
- env `MODE` from ConfigMap `app-config` key `APP_MODE`
- env `EXTRA` from `app-config` key `OPTIONAL_KEY`, marked **optional** (that key doesn't exist — the pod must still start)

Target: `MODE` ← app-config/APP_MODE, and `EXTRA` ← app-config/OPTIONAL_KEY with `optional: true`.
questions.hint: `env` with two entries; the second's `configMapKeyRef` needs `optional: true`. Build with `--dry-run=client -o yaml` and edit.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cfg-env, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: MODE
      valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: APP_MODE } }
    - name: EXTRA
      valueFrom: { configMapKeyRef: { name: app-config, key: OPTIONAL_KEY, optional: true } }
YAML

questions.title: Bulk envFrom with a prefix
questions.teach:
**Bulk → env:** `envFrom: [{configMapRef: {name: cm}}]` injects **every** key as an env var. Add `prefix: CFG_` to namespace them all (`CFG_APP_MODE`…).

**Gotcha:** `envFrom` can't rename individual keys — for that use single-key `valueFrom` instead.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `cfg-envfrom` (`busybox:1.36`, sleep) that bulk-injects **all** keys of ConfigMap `app-config` as env vars with prefix `CFG_`.

Target: `envFrom` references configMapRef `app-config` with `prefix: CFG_`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cfg-envfrom, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    envFrom:
    - prefix: CFG_
      configMapRef: { name: app-config }
YAML

verification.description: cfg-envfrom: envFrom app-config with prefix CFG_

questions.title: ConfigMap as a volume (items)
questions.teach:
**As a volume:** each ConfigMap key becomes a file under the mountPath. Use `items: [{key: K, path: p}]` to expose **only** specific keys, renamed to the given paths.

**Gotcha:** with `items`, keys you don't list are NOT mounted — only the selected files appear.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `cfg-vol` (`busybox:1.36`, sleep) that mounts ConfigMap `app-config` as a volume at `/etc/config`, exposing **only** key `APP_MODE` as a file named `mode`.

Target: a configMap volume (`app-config`) mounted at `/etc/config` with `items` mapping `APP_MODE` → `mode`.
questions.hint: Volume: `configMap: {name: app-config, items: [{key: APP_MODE, path: mode}]}`; mount it at `/etc/config`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: cfg-vol, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts: [ { name: cfg, mountPath: /etc/config } ]
  volumes:
  - name: cfg
    configMap:
      name: app-config
      items: [ { key: APP_MODE, path: mode } ]
YAML

verification.description: cfg-vol: configMap app-config volume at /etc/config, item APP_MODE→mode

questions.title: Secret as env + as a mounted volume
questions.teach:
Secrets consume like ConfigMaps (swap `configMap*`→`secret*`): `secretKeyRef` for a single env var, and a **volume** (`secret: {secretName: s}`) where each key is a file. `defaultMode: 0400` restricts file perms.

**Gotcha:** octal file modes show as **decimal** in the API — `0400` reads back as `256`.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `sec-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, sleep):
- env `KEY` from Secret `app-secret` key `API_KEY`
- mount Secret `app-secret` as a volume at `/etc/secret` with `defaultMode: 0400`

Target: `KEY` ← app-secret/API_KEY; a secret volume (`app-secret`) at `/etc/secret` with defaultMode `0400`.
questions.hint: env uses `secretKeyRef`; the volume is `secret: {secretName: app-secret, defaultMode: 0400}`. (0400 shows as 256 in the API.)
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: sec-pod, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: KEY
      valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: app-secret, key: API_KEY } }
    volumeMounts: [ { name: sec, mountPath: /etc/secret } ]
  volumes:
  - name: sec
    secret:
      secretName: app-secret
      defaultMode: 0400
YAML

verification.description: sec-pod: env KEY←app-secret/API_KEY + secret volume at /etc/secret (mode 0400)

questions.title: Immutable ConfigMap
questions.teach:
`immutable: true` locks a ConfigMap/Secret so its data can't be edited. Set it in YAML, or on an existing object with `kubectl patch configmap x -p '{"immutable":true}'`.

**Gotcha:** you can't un-set it — to change an immutable object you must **delete + recreate** it.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create an **immutable** ConfigMap `locked-config` with data `FOO=bar`.

Target: ConfigMap `locked-config` has `data.FOO=bar` and `immutable: true`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ckad-config create configmap locked-config --from-literal=FOO=bar`, then `kubectl -n ckad-config patch configmap locked-config -p '{"immutable":true}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n ckad-config create configmap locked-config --from-literal=FOO=bar
kubectl -n ckad-config patch configmap locked-config -p '{"immutable":true}'

questions.title: Projected volume (combine sources)
questions.teach:
A **projected** volume combines multiple sources — `configMap`, `secret`, `downwardAPI` — into ONE directory at a single mountPath. Each source lists its own `items`.

**Gotcha:** all sources share one directory, so two sources writing the same `path` collide.
questions.prompt:
In `ckad-config`, create pod `proj-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, sleep) with a **projected** volume mounted at `/etc/proj` combining three sources:
- ConfigMap `app-config` (item `APP_MODE` → `mode`)
- Secret `app-secret` (item `API_KEY` → `key`)
- downwardAPI (`metadata.name` → `podname`)

Target: a projected volume at `/etc/proj` with all three sources.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: proj-pod, namespace: ckad-config }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts: [ { name: proj, mountPath: /etc/proj } ]
  volumes:
  - name: proj
    projected:
      sources:
      - configMap: { name: app-config, items: [ { key: APP_MODE, path: mode } ] }
      - secret: { name: app-secret, items: [ { key: API_KEY, path: key } ] }
      - downwardAPI: { items: [ { path: podname, fieldRef: { fieldPath: metadata.name } } ] }
YAML

verification.description: proj-pod: projected volume at /etc/proj (configMap + secret + downwardAPI)

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod stuck on config
questions.teach:
A pod referencing a **missing** ConfigMap key stays in **CreateContainerConfigError**. `kubectl describe pod

` Events show `couldn't find key in ConfigMap`; patch it in: `kubectl patch configmap … -p '{"data":{"K":"v"}}'`. **Gotcha:** fix the ConfigMap, not the pod — the kubelet retries and starts the container, **no pod recreate** needed.
questions.prompt:
Pod `brokencfg` in `ckad-config` is **not Running** — it's stuck because of a config reference. Diagnose and fix it so it runs. Do **not** delete the pod.

Target: pod `brokencfg` is `Running`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ckad-config describe pod brokencfg` → 'couldn't find key GREETING in ConfigMap app-config'. Add that key: `kubectl -n ckad-config patch configmap app-config -p '{"data":{"GREETING":"hello"}}'`.
questions.solution:
# describe shows: couldn't find key GREETING in ConfigMap app-config
kubectl -n ckad-config patch configmap app-config -p '{"data":{"GREETING":"hello"}}'
# kubelet retries and the pod starts within a few seconds
kubectl -n ckad-config get pod brokencfg

verification.description: brokencfg is Running (missing ConfigMap key fixed at the source)
